**Visual analysis:**

- Plant: Tomato compound leaf/branch
- Overall leaf color: pale/yellowish-green, notably chlorotic
- Multiple scattered brown spots of small-to-medium size on several leaves
- One leaflet (far left) shows extensive marginal/tip necrosis (dead brown tissue)
- No visible white fuzzy growth (rules out Late Blight, Gray Mold)
- No obvious concentric rings on lesions (argues against Early Blight)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- Spots appear circular to irregular with darker brown borders on a pale/tan center

**Reasoning:**

The combination of pale/yellowing leaves with multiple small circular-to-irregular tan/brown lesions scattered across the leaf surface, progressing from older leaves with some becoming fully necrotic, best matches **Septoria Leaf Blotch**. The lesion description fits: "Circular, tan to gray lesions... dark-brown perimeter with possible yellow halo; water-soaked appearance on leaf undersides; lesions smaller than early blight and lack concentric rings." The general chlorosis and spotting pattern is consistent with Septoria progressing from lower/older leaves.

Early Blight was considered but lacks visible concentric rings. Late Blight was considered but no water-soaked or greasy appearance with white sporulation is visible. The spots are too scattered and uniform for Late Blight's larger patches.
